statement: Rent controls should be expanded to cover more rental units.

passages.title: BC Greens focus on renters and childcare as NDP and Conservatives roll out economic plans (Victoria Buzz)
passages.quote: Under vacancy control, allowable rent increases would be tied to a rental unit rather than the individual tenant. passages.title: BC Greens announce plan to support renters, unveil two new candidates for South Island
passages.quote: Currently, rental increases are allowed once per year—unless there is a change of tenant. Vacancy control ties increases in rent to a unit, rather than a tenant, reducing the incentive for landlords to evict tenants without fault. Annual increases will continue to be determined by the Residential Tenancy Branch. Amend the Residential Tenancy Act to prohibit blanket no pets clauses in rental contracts.

passages.title: Emily Lowan's BC Greens promise to bring back vacancy control (Daily Hive)
passages.quote: That’s why the BC Greens are stepping up with a plan to deliver affordability for renters and protect them from the people trying to profit off of the housing crisis.” Vacancy control In B.C., landlords and property managers are allowed to increase rent for current tenants once per year . However, once that tenant leaves, they can then raise the price as much as they want, typically to the market rate. “Vacancy control ties increases in rent to a unit, rather than a tenant, reducing the incentive for landlords to evict tenants without fault,” reads the BC Greens’ policy brief. They said that the Residential Tenancy Branch would continue to determine annual increases.

passages.title: Emily Lowan's BC Greens promise to bring back vacancy control (Daily Hive)
passages.quote: “In 1973, BC NDP Premier Dave Barrett passed vacancy control, which ties allowable rent increases to units, not individual tenants, to fight a spiralling cost-of-living crisis and low vacancy rates. It was effective and popular, yet was stripped away by the following conservative government,” said Lowan. In 2025, the BC Greens introduced a bill to bring vacancy control back to the province, but it was unsuccessful. In 2023, Daily Hive Urbanized asked then-Housing Minister Ravi Kahlon his thoughts on this tool for keeping rent costs down, and he said that their approach was instead to build more housing supply.

passages.title: BC Greens 2026: Our Plan for British Columbia (platform)
passages.quote: The BC Greens will: Build and protect 26,000 permanently affordable, non-market homes a year, and make it easier and quicker to build all forms of housing. Make transit fast, frequent, and free. Pass vacancy control to ensure landlords can’t raise the rent every time a tenant moves out. Restart the stalled $10-a-day childcare pledge as we chart a path towards universal coverage, with fair pay for early childhood educators.
